## Glossary

**CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS**  
Claude Code's concurrent subagent cap, raised by ClaudeInSessionDecisions to the user's cap (20 when unset) plus maxSubagents (76).

**cold miss**  
Codex: a key with no primed thread runs the decision inline on a fresh thread and primes in the background.

**cycle**  
One decision on a branch of the primed state, discarded afterwards; no cycle sees another's turns.

**DecisionError**  
A failed decision: reason, dispatch ('not-dispatched' or 'attempted') and whether the turn is settled.

**DecisionRequest**  
Per-decision input: input, timeoutMs, signal, onAdmission, outputSchema (Codex), group (ClaudeSubagentSessions) and standby (both Claude subagent implementations).

**dispatcher generation**  
ClaudeInSessionDecisions: a foundry-dispatch agent that starts members, replaced once its context passes recycleTokens.

**fan-out**  
ClaudeSubagentSessions: one dispatcher turn calling Agent once per batched member, each prompt replaced by a PreToolUse hook.

**hedgeAfterMs**  
Codex only: after this delay the same input starts on a second branch; the first to finish wins.

**onAdmission**  
Callback run before the native write, so the caller can register the admission.

**orphan**  
An in-session member whose dispatcher ended unasked; never retired, its answer call held for the session's life, capped by maxOrphans.

**perTaskStopAffordance**  
Declared by ClaudeCodeSession when an extension is attached, so the user's Stop spares background agents.

**prime**  
The one cold step: role instructions plus stable context and a primer turn, which becomes the cached prefix.

**primed key**  
Foundry's auxiliary session identity ${threadId}:aux:${role}, optionally with a phase tag.

**primed-claude**  
Class: ClaudePrimedSessions, a persisted primed Claude session resumed with --fork-session per cycle from a pre-spawned spare.

**primed-claude-in-session**  
Class: ClaudeInSessionDecisions, roles as subagents inside the main ClaudeCodeSession: dispatchers, recycle, orphans, subagent cap.

**primed-claude-subagents**  
Class: ClaudeSubagentSessions, roles as subagents of a dedicated CLI process per group, fan-out batching, side sessions, standby spares.

**primed-codex**  
Class: CodexPrimedSessions, one app-server per account, thread/fork per cycle, private CODEX_HOME, hedging and service tier.

**primed-contract**  
Class: the PrimedSessions contract every implementation shares: decide, evict, limits, snapshot, close, branch per cycle, re-prime by primeHash, DecisionRequest and DecisionError.

**PrimedSessions**  
The contract in src/primed.ts: decide(spec, request), evict(key), limits(), snapshot(), close(), optional prestart/releaseGroup; prime(spec) is CodexPrimedSessions only, and maxConcurrent / maxBackgroundPrimes are implementation config.

**primeHash**  
A spec's identity: its explicit hash, else sha256 of instructions and context; a change re-primes.

**PrimeSpec**  
What a key is primed with: key, instructions, context and an optional hash.

**private CODEX_HOME**  
A Codex home the caller passes through env, holding only the login (auth.json linked, not copied), so the user's AGENTS.md, memories and MCP servers never reach a decision.

**serviceTier**  
Codex only, opt-in fast tier: lower latency, may consume usage faster.

**side session**  
An extra CLI process of a ClaudeSubagentSessions group: a fan-out one (at most maxSessionsPerGroup, 6) or a standby one.

**spare**  
A pre-started fork or subagent waiting for exactly one decision.

**standby**  
Context a spare is pre-started with; a decision whose standby equals it takes the spare with no dispatch.

**text-only**  
Codex and ClaudePrimedSessions decisions run with tools, plugins and project instructions disabled; subagent members may call only their own decision tools. Other tool activity fails the decision or recycles the process.

**volatile key**  
A key whose primed context was replaced before it ever served; it primes again only once its context repeats.

## 1. What this Warden covers

Decision roles (middleware such as Wardens and guards) served by one warm session per role: primed once with role instructions and stable context, branched for each decision and the branch discarded, behind the shared PrimedSessions contract with four runtime implementations.

## 2. The domain

Callers program against the PrimedSessions contract (src/primed.ts): `decide(spec, request)` with a PrimeSpec keyed `${threadId}:aux:${role}` (plus a phase tag when one role runs under several instructions), `evict(key)` to drop a key's primed session (a no-op on the subagent implementations), and `limits()`, `snapshot()` and `close()`; CodexPrimedSessions also has `prime(spec)` to warm a key ahead of its first decision. A key re-primes only when `primeHash` changes (its explicit hash, else sha256 of instructions and context), after eviction (idle, capacity past maxSessions, or evict()) or after process loss. A DecisionRequest carries `input`, optional `timeoutMs`, a `signal` that cancels a waiting or running decision, `onAdmission`, which runs before the native write, `outputSchema` (Codex only), `group` (ClaudeSubagentSessions) and `standby` (ClaudeSubagentSessions and ClaudeInSessionDecisions: it matches a pre-started spare, else it is sent in front of `input`). A failure is a DecisionError that says whether anything was dispatched and whether the turn is settled. Blocked limits refuse before dispatch, and there is no fallback and no retry. On CodexPrimedSessions and ClaudePrimedSessions `maxConcurrent` (default 8 and 1) bounds decisions across keys, and decisions on one key run concurrently.

Pick the implementation by runtime and process shape. CodexPrimedSessions runs one `codex app-server` per account, hosts every key as a persisted thread and forks it per cycle (restating the instructions), on a private CODEX_HOME the caller supplies through `env`, holding only the login; a thread reporting any instruction source is refused. Only it has `hedgeAfterMs` and `serviceTier`. ClaudePrimedSessions persists a text-only primed Claude session and resumes it with `--fork-session` per cycle from a pre-spawned spare. ClaudeSubagentSessions serves a group's (a thread's) roles as subagents of a dedicated CLI process. Decisions arriving within `batchWindowMs` (25) are batched into one dispatcher turn (`maxMembers` 12, split across up to `maxSessionsPerGroup` 6 fan-out side sessions), or served from standby spares (`sparesPerRole` 2, `prestart`, `idleMs` 30 min). ClaudeInSessionDecisions keeps the roles inside the main ClaudeCodeSession (installed with `session.extend(decisions)` before start), so a thread and its roles are one process. It raises CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS to the user's cap (20 when unset) plus `maxSubagents` (76), with `dispatchers` 1, `sparesPerRole` 1, `recycleTokens` 100k and `maxOrphans` 40.

These are not general sessions. None is a general agent: Codex and ClaudePrimedSessions decisions run text-only, the subagent implementations let members call only their own decision tools, and other tool activity fails the decision or recycles the process, so an ordinary agent turn belongs on a HarnessSession transport. Not here: creating and driving ordinary sessions and the ClaudeCodeSession / CodexAppServerSession transports themselves (transports); gating the main agent's own tool calls (tool-gates-and-secrets); choosing accounts, reading rate limits and pooling logins (pools-routing-limits); token counts and subagent events on onEvent (session-contract).

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#primed-decision-sessions -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Primed decision sessions (in "@inixiative/agent-session")

#### Primed decision sessions

One live, warm session per middleware role, primed once with its role
instructions and stable context, reset to that primed state every cycle:

```ts
import { CodexPrimedSessions } from "@inixiative/agent-session";

const decisions = new CodexPrimedSessions({ model: "gpt-6-luna", effort: "low", cwd: privateDir });
const result = await decisions.decide(
  { key: `${threadId}:aux:domain:api`, instructions: rolePrompt, context: layerContent, hash: layerHash },
  { input: "## Message\n…", onAdmission: register },
);
```

Run Codex decisions on a private `CODEX_HOME` that holds only the login (link
`auth.json` from the account's home; a copy forks its refresh token): Codex has no
setting that drops the user's own `AGENTS.md`, and a decision thread that reports
any instruction source is refused.

Codex hosts every key as a thread of one `app-server` process per account and
forks the primed thread per cycle; Claude forks a persisted primed session with
a pre-spawned spare. Measured on a ChatGPT login: warm Codex decisions 2.45 s
median vs 3.9 s for `codex exec` per decision, with 34% fewer input tokens; warm
Claude (haiku) decisions 1.95 s with the whole primed prefix read from cache.

##### In the main session's own process (Claude)

`ClaudeInSessionDecisions` holds decision roles as subagents of a main
`ClaudeCodeSession`, so a thread and all its decision roles are one process:

```ts
const decisions = new ClaudeInSessionDecisions({ model: "claude-haiku-5-5", effort: "low" });
const session = new ClaudeCodeSession({ model: "claude-opus-5-5", cwd, toolGate: true });
session.extend(decisions); // before start(): agents, an SDK MCP server, a PreToolUse claim
await session.start();     // one internal setup turn starts the root agent
decisions.prestart(threadId, roles.map((spec) => ({ spec, standby })));
await decisions.ready();
const result = await decisions.decide(spec, { input, standby });
```

- **Shape.** The setup turn asks the main model to start `foundry-root` in the
  background. The root never ends: it starts dispatcher generations
  (`foundry-dispatch`), which start members (`foundry-warden`), all in the
  background, through a `next` tool the host holds open. A member holds the
  host's `moment` tool until a decision answers it, and answers through
  `answer`. After setup, no member activity needs a main-model turn.
- **Pinned input.** Every spawn passes the session's PreToolUse callback,
  which replaces its prompt with the composed text, so agent definitions are
  generic and an edited role reaches the next spare without a relaunch.
  Spawns of these agent types from anywhere else are denied; the main agent's
  own subagents go to the tool gate untouched.
- **Fresh per call.** Each member serves one decision. A used one is replaced
  at once; a role with no held spare starts a member with its input inline.
- **Slices.** `dispatchers` (default 1) splits the roles into fixed slices,
  each started by its own dispatcher, so refills are written at once. A
  dispatcher writes one Agent call per member as output tokens: one
  dispatcher refilled 75 members in ~20 s (2026-11-02). A role keeps its
  slice while it is wanted; a new role joins the smallest.
- **Recycle.** A dispatcher's context grows ~700 tokens per member started;
  past `recycleTokens` (100k) a new generation of its slice takes over and
  the old one ends into the root once empty.
- **Orphans.** A nested agent whose parent ended reports its own end to the
  main thread, which wakes the main model (Claude Code 2.1.300). Members of a
  dispatcher that ended unasked are therefore never retired or stopped, and an
  orphan's `answer` call is held for the session's life. Past `maxOrphans`
  (40) `serving()` turns false and `setup` reports `degraded`; `decide()` does
  not refuse on its own, so the caller checks `serving()` and falls back.
- **Limits.** Claude Code runs 20 subagents at once by default; the launch
  raises `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` to the user's own cap (20 when
  unset) plus `maxSubagents` (76), so 96 by default. The
  session declares `perTaskStopAffordance`, so the user's Stop spares
  background agents.

<!-- unit doc:docs/transports-pools-routing.md#primed-decision-sessions -->
**Source:** `docs/transports-pools-routing.md` § Primed decision sessions (in "Transports, primed sessions, pools and routing")

#### Primed decision sessions

One live, warm session per middleware role. The key is Foundry's auxiliary
session identity (`${threadId}:aux:${role}`), optionally extended with a phase
tag when one role runs under several instructions.

- **Prime** once: role instructions (developer/system role) plus the stable
  context (layer content, user role, as data). That primed state is the cached prefix.
- **Per cycle**: branch from the primed state, run the decision, discard the
  branch. One cycle never sees another's turns.
- **Re-prime** only when the prime hash changes (default: sha256 of
  instructions and context; callers pass layer content hashes), after idle
  eviction, or after process loss. Those are the only cold paths, and on Codex
  they stay off the decision's critical path: a miss runs the decision inline on
  a fresh thread (context + input, same instructions) and primes in the
  background. A key whose primed context is replaced before it ever served is
  volatile and primes again only once its context repeats. On Codex,
  `prime(spec)` primes a key ahead of its first decision.
- **Concurrency**: decisions on one key run concurrently (forks are independent);
  priming is deduplicated per key and context. `maxBackgroundPrimes` (Codex,
  default 2) bounds primer turns outside the decision slots.
- **Hedging** (`hedgeAfterMs`, Codex): a decision still running after the
  threshold starts the same input on a second branch; the first to finish wins
  and the other is interrupted off the result path (`hedged` / `hedge-settled`
  events). It trims per-request tails for a duplicate request on the slow
  fraction; it cannot help when the provider stalls every request at once.
- **Service tier** (`serviceTier`, Codex, opt-in): gpt-6-luna `fast` measured
  p50 2.23 s vs 2.52 s with no tier; it may consume usage faster.

| | Codex (`CodexPrimedSessions`) | Claude (`ClaudePrimedSessions`) |
|---|---|---|
| Process | one `codex app-server` per account hosts every key as a thread | one CLI process per conversation |
| Prime | persisted `thread/start` + primer turn | persisted text-only session + primer turn |
| Reset | `thread/fork` (ephemeral) through the primer turn, restating the instructions | `--resume <primed> --fork-session --no-session-persistence` |
| Warm path | fork ≈ 60–90 ms, then the turn | pre-spawned spare fork: no process start |
| Cleanup | fork unsubscribed; primed thread deleted on eviction/close; orphans in the private cwd swept at start | forks write no history; the primed transcript is deleted on eviction/close, and leftovers for the private cwd are swept on first use |
| Text-only | features, plugins, notify, project docs, tool instructions disabled; read-only sandbox; approvals never; run on a private `CODEX_HOME` holding only the login (the user's AGENTS.md, memories and MCP servers live in theirs) | `--safe-mode --tools "" --strict-mcp-config …` |
| Violations | a thread reporting `instructionSources` → refused before any turn; non-text item, MCP startup or server request → interrupt, recycle process | tool activity → decision fails |

Why fork and not rollback: codex-cli 0.155.1 refuses rollback on both thread
kinds (above), and ephemeral threads cannot be forked ("no rollout found"), so
the primed thread is persisted and each cycle forks it. A fork that does not
restate `baseInstructions`/`developerInstructions` runs on Codex's default
prompt (10.8k instead of 6.6k input tokens) and misses the cache.

A violation or an unacknowledged interrupt recycles the Codex process: every
decision in flight on it fails at once (`transport`), and the next decision on
each key re-primes on a fresh process.

Decisions on one key run concurrently on both runtimes and are bounded across keys
(`maxConcurrent`: 8 on Codex, 1 on Claude); only priming is serialized per key. Claude: the first decision
takes the key's spare fork, an overlapping one starts its own fork (a process
start, no re-prime), and one spare is kept afterwards. A key replaced or evicted
while decisions still fork from it keeps its primed transcript until the last one
finishes.
`DecisionRequest.signal` cancels: a waiting decision is refused before dispatch,
a running one is interrupted and reports settlement from the acknowledgment or
the process exit.
`onAdmission` runs before the native write; `DecisionError` states whether
anything was dispatched and whether the turn is settled (terminal observed or
process exit observed). Blocked limits refuse before dispatch; there is no
fallback and no retry.

<!-- unit doc:docs/transports-pools-routing.md#claude-subagent-decisions-claudesubagentsessions -->
**Source:** `docs/transports-pools-routing.md` § Claude subagent decisions (`ClaudeSubagentSessions`) (in "Transports, primed sessions, pools and routing")

#### Claude subagent decisions (`ClaudeSubagentSessions`)

One Claude CLI process per group (a Foundry thread) serves its decision roles as subagents, instead of a process per role. Each role is a custom agent (`--agents`) whose system prompt is the base instructions, the role's instructions and its stable context, read from the prompt cache. Decisions of a group arriving within `batchWindowMs` (25 ms) fan out in one dispatcher turn (`--tools Agent`, on the configured `model`): the dispatcher calls the Agent tool once per listed member, and a PreToolUse hook replaces each call's prompt with that member's exact input and denies any call it cannot match. Members settle on their own task frames (`task_notification`, the subagent's forwarded text), so a decision never waits for the dispatcher's wrap-up, which is interrupted once every member answered; the turn is then rewound (`rewind_conversation`), so each fan-out starts from an empty conversation. A member the dispatcher skipped is sent in one more fan-out, then refused unsent. A deadline or abort refuses an unsent member and stops a running subagent (`stop_task`). Batches above `maxMembers` (12, measured: all answers at 3.9 s for 8, 4.4 s for 12, 7.9 s for 23) split evenly across up to `maxSessionsPerGroup` (6) fan-out side sessions, which also serve overlapping fan-outs. A changed role definition starts a side session holding it. Measured 2026-10-12 (CLI 2.1.296): one side session is about 210 MB idle and 300–320 MB with 23 subagents running.

**Pre-started members (`prestart`, `DecisionRequest.standby`).** A group can keep its roles pre-started, so a decision starts without any dispatch. Each role also has a standby variant whose only tool is `mcp__foundry__moment`, served by the host as an SDK MCP server over the control channel (`mcp_message`). A standby fan-out (foreground, off any decision's path) starts every role with the group's standby context (in Foundry, the thread's own context, refreshed when a turn lands). Each member calls `moment` at once, and the host holds the call open (`MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` set to a day). A decision whose `standby` equals a spare's context is admitted, then answers that call with its `input`, so all such members continue in parallel with no dispatcher on the path. A spare serves one decision, which keeps each call fresh: what is pre-started is the composed context, never an earlier conversation. Each role keeps `sparesPerRole` (2) spares, each copy in its own standby side session, so a burst of decisions on one role (several guards in one turn) is served while the used copy refills. A decision takes the spare whose side session has the fewest free spares left, so a trigger empties whole side sessions. Refills are staggered so one copy of every role is always serving: used copies refill in a free standby side session (at most two beyond the full copy sets), while a partly used standby turn keeps serving its unused spares. It ends, and its side session is reused, once every spare is done, or once nothing it serves is in flight and every role it still holds has another held copy. New standby context retires the old spares (their turn ends once no decision uses them). A decision with no matching spare fans out with the standby context in front of its input, in a fan-out side session: standby side sessions never take a fan-out, and `maxSessionsPerGroup` bounds fan-out side sessions only. A group idle for `idleMs`, or released (`releaseGroup`, a closed thread), lets its spares go.

Measured live 2026-10-14 (CLI 2.1.299, Haiku 5.5, 25 roles, `maxMembers` 6, `scripts/measure-subagents.ts`): a trigger on all 25 served by spares took 2.5 s the first time, 1.7 s after a hold and 1.8 s after new standby context, against 7.2 s for a fan-out; 15 processes (10 standby, 5 fan-out), 3.9 GB in all.
